S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor: Edgar’s divorce forced him to divide a long-shared household, personal archives, family photographs, and cultural materials that carried deep meaning for him. During that transition, intrusive doubts about whether he had handled decisions correctly or harmed important relationships began to recur, and he tried to quiet them through repeated reviewing of messages, records, and mental reconstructions of conversations. The cycle gradually interfered with his systems architecture work, delayed mentorship commitments, and made preparation for community workshops feel far more burdensome than it had in the past. He eventually asked his primary-care clinician for a psychiatric referral after a coding workshop for Indigenous youth was disrupted by the amount of time he spent trying to settle the same doubts before leaving home.

S065.manifestation: Even when I’m trying to work through a system design or prepare a lesson, this thought keeps barging in that I may have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, mishandled some family photos, or let someone in the community down, and I can’t seem to let it pass even though I know I’ve been over it already.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: I came in because I keep losing chunks of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and mentally replaying conversations before I leave the house or start work, like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My work has slowed down enough that I’ve missed design milestones and had to postpone mentoring sessions I used to handle reliably. I also felt embarrassed when I was late and unprepared for a youth coding workshop that mattered to me.
